subject: Post-call follow-up: Cirrus Health integration constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@cirrushealth.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call follow-up: Cirrus Health integration constraints & next steps

Thanks for your time today, Alyssa — quick recap + suggested next steps so we’re aligned. I’ve included Monica and Ben from our team for technical/solutions follow-through.

Top pain points you highlighted
- Latency sensitivity for ED triage workflows (p95 target < 350ms for short prompts).
- Must not send PHI to a shared tenancy; any PII/PHI needs either on-prem handling or VPC private deployment.
- Need structured, discrete outputs for EHR ingestion (JSON with coded fields) rather than free-text notes.
- Reranking of candidate suggestions (embeddings + reranker) to prioritize hospital-approved protocols.

Goals we agreed on
- PoC to validate latency and structured-output reliability for 10k daily triage requests.
- Technical deep-dive (30–45m) with engineering next Wednesday (availability suggested below).
- Procurement will need SOC 2 + KMS/HSM details for evaluation.

Integration / product fit notes
- Streaming + function-calling for incremental triage updates will likely be required (reduce client-perceived latency).
- Embedding+rerank flow looks like the best fit for suggestion prioritization; we'll propose a quantized model variant for cost control.
- SDK changes: small wrapper to emit structured JSON objects from the model with strict schema enforcement. We can provide a reference adapter.

Immediate asks (from us to you)
1) Can you share a small sanitized sample of the triage payload (3–5 records) and the target output schema?
2) Will procurement accept a private VPC deployment + customer-managed KMS, or do we need an on-prem appliance?
3) Confirm windows for the technical deep-dive: we suggested Thu 11/05 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 11/06 08:00–09:00 PT.

Attachments: redwood-integration-onepager.pdf (high-level fit), streaming-funcall-proposal.docx (example flow and estimated latency impact).

Next on our side: Monica will draft a short technical checklist to scope the PoC and Ben will pull a pricing sketch for a dedicated pool vs hosted with VPC.

Thanks again — I’ll follow up after you confirm availability.

Regards,
Markus Klein

Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: Cirrus Health integration constraints & next steps

Thanks Markus — appreciated the clear summary. Quick clarifications and answers below.

- Sample data: I can share 5 de-identified triage records (fyi they’re unstructured free-text + some structured metadata). I’ll upload them to the secure S3 link by EOD.
- Deployment: Procurement has indicated they prefer a customer VPC with customer-managed KMS. On-prem is a possibility but will require longer procurement lead time.
- SOC 2: We need a copy of your SOC 2 Type II report and a short security FAQ for our legal team.
- Pricing: procurement asked for a ballpark (monthly) for a dedicated pool vs hosted burstable. If you can include a rough delta that would help speed review.

Deep-dive windows: Thu 11/05 10:00–11:00 PT works for engineering — please send calendar invite.

Alyssa

Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Cirrus PoC scoping checklist (draft)

Markus / Ben — draft checklist to bring to the deep-dive. I’ll surface this to Alyssa as a prep note before the call.

1) Data ingress
- Confirm sanitized sample format (Alyssa to upload S3 link).
- Determine whether we perform on-the-fly redaction client-side or in a private deployment.

2) Latency targets & measurement
- Define p50/p95 targets and representative prompt lengths.
- Add synthetic microbenchmarks against expected prompt distributions.

3) Structured output schema
- Need explicit field list + validation rules (e.g., ICD codes, severity scores).
- Plan: SDK adapter will validate and reject outputs that fail schema; fallback to model with higher sampling temperature disabled.

4) Streaming & function-calling
- Implementation: continuous streaming with intermediate function callbacks for partial data persistence.
- Risk: model hallucination in partial outputs — mitigate with schema-first prompting + conservative decoding.

5) Embedding + rerank
- Prototype: local embedding store + commercial reranker. Estimate: 40–60ms additional per request for rerank on a 10-candidate set.

6) Security & compliance
- Provide SOC 2 report, KMS details, and SAML/SSO integration notes.

Owners: Monica — schema/SDK adapter, Ben — infra/pricing, Markus — customer-facing coordination + SOW draft.

I’ll attach this as a pre-read to the invite.

—Monica
